text: 4 WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, Module 5: Management of tuberculosis in children and adolescents Figure 1: Cascade of care in children and adolescents exposed to and with TB, with broad topics of PICO questions with corresponding numbers as per section 1.3.1 Un/misdiagnosed Susceptible Preventive treatment Diseased Did NOT access health care system Feeling ill Diagnosed Treated Accessed health care system Exposed Accessed health care system Infected Treatment of DS-TB, DR-TB and TBM (PICO 3, 4a and 4b, and 5) Screening in health care facilities (PICO 1) Diagnostic approaches (PICO 2 a and b) Models of Care TB case detection and TB prevention (PICO 6 a and b) Source: Roadmap towards ending TB in children and adolescents. Second edition. Geneva: World Health Organization; 2018. DS/DR-TB: drug-susceptible/drug-resistant TB; TBM: TB meningitis. Based on this understanding of the cascade of TB care in children and adolescents, the potential contribution of interventions targeting different steps in this cascade is summarized in the following logic model (which was the model used to frame these guidelines) with the potential contribution of the evidence to short-term and long-term outcomes (Figure 2). Figure 2: The logic model used for the guidelines on the management of TB in children and adolescents Inputs • Stakeholder engagement from all sectors in the community • Financial resources • Human resources • Equipment and supplies • Participation by families with children and adolescents exposed to or with (presumptive) TB • Community participation • Infection control at community level • Evidence from research Activities • Contact investigation • TB screening activities • Diagnostic approaches for relevant forms of DS- and DR-TB • Optimal treatment regimens for the treatment of DS- and DR-TB • Innovative models of care to deliver TB services to children and adolescents • Capacity building of health care workers at all levels • Demand generation at community level Short-term outcomes* • Earlier and increased detection of DS- and DR-TB in children and adolescents (1, 2, 6) • Improved TB treatment outcomes (3, 4, 5) • Increase in TB preventive treatment coverage in children and adolescents (6) • Improved quality of child and adolescent TB care (6) Long-term outcomes* • Reduced TB incidence and prevalence in children and adolescents (1, 2, 6) • Reduced TB mortality in children and adolescents (1, 3, 4, 5, 6) • Reduced post-TB sequelae in children and adolescents (4, 5) • Reduced financial losses due to TB, for families and for the community (1, 2, 3, 6) *The numbers under short- and long-term outcomes refer to the PICO questions in section 1.6.1. DS/DR-TB: drug-susceptible/drug-resistant TB.
